language.script_notes: Arabic script, with English alongside: all official road signs are bilingual, with Arabic placed above English. Many shop and company signs are English-first, reflecting the large expatriate population.

road_furniture.km_marker_style: Route shields and directional signs have a distinctive style. Utility poles frequently show striped end sections, though plain silver poles also occur.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs on villas and apartment towers.
architecture.roof_material: Flat concrete, with glass and steel in modern towers.
architecture.wall_construction: Beige and sand-coloured villas behind high walls; early buildings used coral stone, mud brick and palm fronds for insulation and airflow, until the oil boom brought steel and glass; Dubai's skyline of high-rise towers and construction sites is a strong tell.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Sand, beige and cream, with mirrored glass on towers.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Skyscrapers and construction cranes in Dubai; mosques with domes and minarets; gated villa compounds; coral-stone forts and wind-towers in heritage areas.

nature.vegetation: Flat sandy desert with sparse scrub, and date palms planted along streets and in oases for shade; irrigated green lawns in the cities.
nature.terrain: Sandy, dune-covered desert that is rarely perfectly flat, with rocky hills in the eastern suburbs and the Hajar Mountains running alongside the eastern border near Hatta; a low, sandy Gulf coastline.
nature.climate_signature: Extremely hot and hazy for much of the year, with bright light and very little rain.

vehicles.plate_color: Mainly white plates, sometimes with a red strip on the left; Oman, next door, uses yellow plates, and Qatar uses similar colouring.
vehicles.plate_format: Black text on a white plate of 520mm × 110mm, with serial formats that vary by emirate — letters such as D for Dubai and AD for Abu Dhabi — and Arabic and English characters.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Large SUVs such as the Nissan Patrol and Toyota Land Cruiser dominate; the Street View car's white roof is sometimes visible, especially on Sir Bani Yas Island.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: The Street View car's white roof appears occasionally, and on Sir Bani Yas Island it is visible in nearly every panorama.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Gulf desert, Arabic and English signage and the rocky Musandam and Hajar hills
confusion_set.tiebreaker: White plates (sometimes with a red strip) here versus Oman's yellow plates; Oman's blue directional signs and all-red guardrail reflectors differ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar plate colouring and Gulf desert scenery
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The terrain here is rarely perfectly flat and has rocky hills in the east, while Qatar's is uniformly flat.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Arabian desert and Arabic-script signs
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Compare plates and signs directly; the tall Dubai skyline and bilingual Arabic-above-English signs are a strong tell for this country.
